newsitem.title: CANADA: TD-Bank says Ontario ahead on deficit plan.
newsitem.headline: TD-Bank says Ontario ahead on deficit plan.

text.p: The Ontario government is expected to beat its 1996/97 deficit target by a wide margin and may balance the province's books ahead of schedule, the Toronto-Dominion Bank said on Wednesday.
In its outlook for Ontario's 1997/98 budget, TD-Bank said healthy revenue growth would allow the government to proceed with the next stage of its planned 30 percent cut in personal income taxes.
The ruling Conservatives will deliver on May 6 their second full budget since sweeping to power in Canada's most-populous province in 1995.

"The Ontario government will likely record a deficit of less than C$7 billion in fiscal 1996/97, well ahead of the C$8.2 billion target set in its 1996 budget," TD senior economist Teresa Courchene said in a statement.
Courchene said Ontario's healthier economy may allow the government to speed up its timetable for wiping out the budget deficit by 2000/2001.

In a third quarter report last February, Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves said government revenues had grown faster than projected due to higher personal, corporate and retail sales tax revenues resulting from a stronger economy.
"If the economic environment in Ontario remains favourable, the Ontario government may attempt to balance its budget by fiscal 1999-2000, one year ahead of its target date," Courchene said.
She said the healthier economy will likely allow Eves to go ahead with the next stage of Ontario's income tax cut.
Ontario's basic personal income tax rate was lowered to 49 percent from 58 percent of the federal tax rate in last year's budget.
"(It) will likely be reduced further, probably by about 4-4.5 percentage points effective July 1, 1997," Courchene said.
